title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the page and the title of the cote. k0 is a base field with an embedding (place) v: k0 → C. k is a large field over k0; given the transcendence theme it is most plausibly C, or an algebraically closed field of infinite transcendence degree over k0. Gal(k/k0) means Aut(k/k0). M is a motive over k0 (or the tensor category it generates). There are two fibre functors:
- the algebraic (de Rham) realisation ξ_{M,k0} over k0;
- the Betti realisation ξ^Z_{M,v} over Z, attached to v.
G = G_{k0} is the motivic Galois group, viewed inside GL(M_k(∞)), i.e. GL of the Betti realisation at the infinite place v.

The torsor. Let P = Isom^⊗(ξ_{M,k0}, ξ^Z_{M,v} ⊗_Z k0). This is a G-torsor over k0, the 'torseur des périodes'. The comparison isomorphism of No 1 ('comparaison de transcendance', i.e. de Rham–Betti comparison via integration) gives a k-point p of P. Grothendieck phrases this as a trivialisation of P_k.

The cocycle. Gal(k/k0) acts on G(k) in two evident ways: through the coefficients, and by conjugation. The map φ_v(σ) = p^{-1}·σ(p) is therefore a 1-cocycle Gal(k/k0) → G(k). Conversely, the trivial torsor over k with this twisted Galois action descends to the k0-torsor P_{v,k0}, carrying the given point over k. Grothendieck then identifies P intrinsically as the torsor of isomorphisms of fibre functors.

The main assertion. 'The point p of P_k is generic' — i.e. its Zariski closure over k0 is all of P, i.e. the periods satisfy no algebraic relations over k0 beyond those defining P. This is equivalent to saying that the image of Gal(k/k0) under φ_v is Zariski-dense in G.

Why this holds. For k algebraically closed of infinite transcendence degree, the k0-Zariski closure of p is the Zariski closure of its Aut(k/k0)-orbit. That orbit is p·φ_v(Γ), so its closure is p·(closure of φ_v(Γ)). Hence p is generic iff φ_v(Γ) is dense.

The margin note 'π transcendant sur k0' is the test case M = Z(1). There G = G_m, P is the torsor whose period point is 2πi, and genericity is exactly the transcendence of π.

So the page is a formulation of what is now called Grothendieck's period conjecture (period torsor; the period point is generic; dim of the torsor = trdeg of the periods), recast as a Zariski-density statement for a 'Galois cocycle' of Aut(C/k0) with values in the motivic Galois group. The marginal 'À vérifier / OK' suggests he checked the equivalence. The page breaks off at '[N.B. alors tout ceci,'.
errors: The equivalence 'generic point ⇔ Zariski-dense image of φ_v' needs k to be large: algebraically closed, of transcendence degree over k0 at least that of the period field. For k algebraic over k0, or k too small, the closure of the Galois orbit need not be the k0-closure of the point. The page does not state this hypothesis explicitly; it may be in the lost earlier part, or covered by 'à vérifier'.

For non-algebraic k, 'Gal(k/k0)' must be read as Aut(k/k0), not a profinite Galois group. The cocycle is then continuous only in a weak sense, and descent is not ordinary Galois descent. It works here only because P is already defined over k0 as an Isom-torsor of fibre functors, so no descent is really needed.

ideas.what: Torsor of tensor isomorphisms between the de Rham fibre functor over k0 and the Betti fibre functor ⊗ k0, under the motivic Galois group; the comparison isomorphism is a C-point of it
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, as reported by André (Une introduction aux motifs, 2004); also Kontsevich–Zagier 2001 and Ayoub
ideas.where_published: Only a footnote on periods in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966); the torsor formulation is not published by Grothendieck as far as I know

ideas.what: Genericity of the period point in the torsor, i.e. all algebraic relations among periods are motivic
ideas.where_published: 1966 de Rham paper, footnote (abelian varieties / transcendence of periods); unsure about the general form

ideas.what: Recasting genericity as Zariski density of the image of a 1-cocycle Aut(C/k0) → G(C) obtained from the period point
ideas.modern_name: 'Galois theory of periods' / Galois action of Aut(C/k0) on periods vs motivic Galois group
ideas.usually_credited_to: André ('Galois theory, motives and transcendental numbers', 2008/09), Ayoub (relative period conjecture)

ideas.what: Case Z(1): genericity ⇔ π transcendental over k0
ideas.modern_name: Lindemann case of the period conjecture

missed.claim: A manuscript formulation (c. 1969–72) of the period conjecture in torsor form, together with an equivalent reformulation: the image of Aut(C/k0) in the motivic Galois group G(C), via the period cocycle, is Zariski-dense. This is a primary-source witness for a conjecture otherwise known mainly through André's second-hand account. The 'Galois-orbit density' viewpoint anticipates André's Galois theory of periods.
missed.quote: Ce point ainsi donné sur P_k est générique, revient à dire que l'[...] Gal(k/k0) →φ_v G(k) [⊂ GL(M_k(∞))] a une image Zariski-dense.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own wording of the period conjecture. It also shows he viewed the motivic Galois group as the Zariski closure of the action of field automorphisms of C on periods — the perspective later developed by André and Ayoub.

missed.claim: The page breaks off at '[N.B. alors tout ceci,' just as consequences or caveats were about to be drawn. Grothendieck also flags the equivalence 'À vérifier'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The missing continuation might have discussed dependence on v or the field of definition. This would interest historians of the period conjecture.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics of the equivalence is elementary. But the page is direct, dated manuscript evidence of Grothendieck formulating the period conjecture via the period torsor, plus a Galois-cocycle density reformulation that is usually associated with later work (André). The conjecture itself is well known and attributed to him, so this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a discovery.
transcription_corrections: 'avec un objet[?] donné[?] sur k0' is more likely 'avec un point donné sur k' — the next sentence reads 'Ce point ainsi donné sur P_k'.
'Il définit par descente un fibré principal homogène P_{v,k0} sous G_{k0}' — the insertion 'P_{v,k0}' is written above the line.
'le fibré principal des de foncteurs homs des isoms' should read roughly 'le fibré principal des isoms de foncteurs ξ_{M,k0} avec ξ^Z_{M,v} ⊗_Z k0'.
The struck-out word before 'Gal(k/k0) → G(k)' is probably 'l'homomorphisme' (or 'l'application'), not 'adhérence'.
Line 7: '(P_v, G(k))' is crossed out together with 'compatible avec la ...'; this is a deletion, not mathematics.
Margin reads 'À vérifier' with 'OK' below; second margin: 'π transcendant sur k0 ....'
